A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PMARK and include the main paper and Appendices A–I. Text, tables, figures, algorithms, and proofs can be matched despite repagination and some malformed mathematical notation in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark detection, attack robustness, text quality, efficiency, and sensitivity experiments in Section 5 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds paragraph-level paraphrasing results and an example in Appendix D.2.

M1.justification: Appendix D.2 introduces an additional context-dependent seeding variant: channel seeds derive from preceding sentence embeddings using separate orthogonal vectors. v1 uses predefined, position-bound seeds and leaves dynamic seeding for future work. The main sampling and detection algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: C4 and BOOKSUM coverage is retained. v2 adds paragraph-level GPT-3.5-turbo paraphrasing that permits sentence merging and reordering, extending the sentence-level and word-level attack scenarios evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched existing experiments. New Table 4 reuses KGW, UPV, SynthID, and k-SemStamp for the added paragraph attack; it introduces no new baseline and does not remove comparators from the original comparisons.

E3.justification: The added paragraph experiment uses a whole-text rewriting prompt that permits merging and reordering, with context-window size w=3 for the seed variant. Existing sample counts, backbones, generation settings, metrics, and sampling budgets remain unchanged; this is an additional protocol rather than a revision of the original experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 adds a targeted robustness analysis of cross-sentence paraphrasing and a before-and-after example retaining detection. The existing channel/budget analysis, soft-z-test sensitivity experiments, attack evaluations, and Appendix H case studies are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates in Table 1; v2 adds standard deviations for TP@FP=1% throughout that central comparison. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting, although neither the repeated-run count nor the estimation procedure is specified, so additional runs cannot be established.

E6.justification: The original numerical results in Tables 1–3 and the appendix benchmark tables are unchanged, as are the existing plotted results. New Table 4 adds paragraph-attack outcomes: online PMARK's TP@FP=1% ranges from 75.00% to 96.97%, and offline PMARK's from 41.67% to 77.45%. These are new-condition results, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds Theorem 7 and a derivation relating multi-channel robustness and signal-to-noise ratio to channel count under independence assumptions. Appendix F adds Theorem 8, bounding single-channel offline distortion by prior-median imbalance. These substantially extend v1's theoretical scope, which deferred offline-error analysis; the multi-channel offline discussion remains qualitative.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about the proxy-function framework, distortion-free online sampling, multi-channel robustness, and efficient offline approximation. The appendix additions support or extend these claims without redefining the stated core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 acknowledges competitive baseline results in Section 5.2 and adds interpretations of the paragraph-attack results and context-dependent seeds. Appendix F argues that small prior imbalance explains limited offline distortion, replacing v1's deferral of this analysis. Rigorous analysis of the new seed distribution is explicitly left open.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 supplies the exact paragraph-paraphrasing prompt and specifies w=3 for the new experiment, providing concrete reproduction details. Existing Appendix G settings and code/model access information are retained, including the unchanged statement that code will be released.

R1.justification: v2 adds two Tsur et al. works on optimized couplings and low-entropy watermarking, plus Bahri et al.'s black-box watermarking work. Short additions in the introduction and Appendix C discuss quality–detectability trade-offs and candidate-scoring approaches; the broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative structure are retained. v2 adds acknowledgments, divides Appendix D into subsections, inserts explanatory transitions and qualifications, and changes the header from Preprint to an ICLR 2026 publication statement. There is no extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 4 and the displayed attack prompt/example, compresses Table 1 to accommodate light-gray standard deviations, and relocates existing algorithms and appendix displays. Existing plotted figures are retained. Some cardinality symbols disappear from Appendix B equations, introducing visible notation defects.

improvement.justification: The new cross-sentence stress test, reproducible attack prompt, and Table 1 variability reporting make the robustness evidence more informative than in v1. The gains are limited by unspecified uncertainty-estimation details, the conditional or single-channel scope of the added theory, and missing symbols in existing appendix proofs. These additions provide a modest net improvement without fully resolving the paper's theoretical and evaluation limitations.
